teaching: When conventional conceptions are forgotten to be conventional and taken for objective facts that no one questions, narrow-minded bigotry and blind prejudice develop unopposed: bigotry is a closed mind, locked into one way of conceiving things, when our whole view of the world is conditioned by our environment (Tao Te Ching, Chapter 2, Thomas Cleary's notes).
youtube_title: You Can Be Bigoted on the Right, Left or Center
phrases: See, we look | at a very
and we call | it the world,
who can get | out of that

image.note: a shepherd driving his flock at dusk, panning from the sheep to the shepherd, every sheep going the one way: 'conventional conceptions… taken for objective facts that everyone knows and no one questions' (on the join)
The Blind Leading the Blind, the men tumbling into the ditch: 'blind prejudice can develop unopposed… that arrogance, that prejudice, that bias' (covers the join)
a shut 15th-century French door: 'just having a closed mind… not open to new ways of thinking… locked into one fixed way' (covers the join)
Salvator Rosa, a ruined temple overgrown in a rocky landscape: 'the world starts to degenerate' (covers the join)
Teniers, peasants puffing their pipes in an inn: 'smoking was thought to be good for you'
Cole, Schroon Mountain after a storm, the weather turning and the leaves turning: 'these two attitudes have changed… the attitudes we have now will also change'

Winslow Homer, a crowd with every face turned up to the same spectacle: 'conditioned and determined by your environment, what you see on Instagram… TV… TikTok and X… what movies you've seen' (on the false-start join; covers the next join)
Catel, a View of Naples through a Window: one narrow slice of the city framed by curtains: 'a very tiny little slice of the world, and we call it the world'
Sōami, two men on a high terrace gazing out over the whole misty lake: 'look more holistically… can see more clearly' (covers the join; under the end-card dissolve)
